note: TARGET-reload-open.jpg (640x357), read by hand on 2026-10-02 off a 4x crop of x 352..608, y 160..357. The frame shows the gun broken open and held to the RIGHT: the two chamber mouths face the camera close, the barrels run down-LEFT and leave the picture through the bottom edge, the action and then the walnut wrist run away to the lower right, and the bare LEFT hand reaches in from the left with a shell. Four marks, each a different point ALONG the gun, which is what pins an orientation; the left hand is deliberately NOT one of them, because in this frame it has left the forend to feed a shell and its own offset is a separate dial (newGun.reload.left) rather than one of the six numbers this fits.

readings.StandingBreech: the mid-point of the two chamber mouths, source px (491, 221). The PART's own centre sits a little below that, so this mark carries about 0.04 of the frame in error and the weight is what says it is still the most certain one.
readings.Action: the metal block behind the breech, with the top lever on it, source px (502, 272).
readings.Forend: the mid-point of the visible barrel band, source px (434, 295); the forend is bolted to the barrels and is about a third of the way down them, and the tube is one dark band in this frame, so this is the best reading of it.
readings.Stock: the walnut wrist running to the lower right, source px (552, 335).
readings.Muzzle: off the bottom edge: the barrel band leaves the frame at source px (412, 357).
